short: A catastrophic defeat for the Italian army, leading to a massive retreat and nearly knocking Italy out of the war.
full:
On 24 October 1917, Austro-Hungarian and German forces launched a surprise offensive against the Italian lines along the Isonzo river near Caporetto. Employing advanced infiltration tactics and an intensive bombardment of poison gas, the Central Powers quickly shattered the Italian defenses. The Italian Second Army dissolved into a chaotic retreat, losing vast amounts of artillery and equipment.

The Italians were forced to fall back nearly a hundred miles to the Piave river, where they finally stabilized the front with the aid of British and French reinforcements. The disaster cost Italy over 300,000 casualties, most of whom were taken prisoner, and prompted a radical reorganization of the Italian high command and civilian government to sustain the war effort.
